overview: Ethiopia's women's health innovation ecosystem sits at the intersection of a large public-health apparatus and a nascent private startup layer. The state anchors most progress through the electronic community health information system (eCHIS), which puts maternal and reproductive health tools in the hands of tablet-equipped health extension workers across roughly 8,000 health posts. Alongside it, a thin but growing femtech scene has emerged, led by YeneHealth, the country's first femtech startup, and a cluster of menstrual health social enterprises such as Mela for Her, Adey Pads and Mariam Seba. Startup activity remains early-stage relative to Ethiopia's population, but the 2025 Startup Proclamation and rising pan-African femtech funding signal a strengthening environment.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent milestones center on YeneHealth's fundraising, national maternal-health gains from digitization, and new pitch platforms for women-led health startups.

items.text: YeneHealth, Ethiopia's first femtech startup, secures a pre-seed investment from Swedish women's health fund The Case for Her to expand sexual and reproductive health services.
YeneHealth raises pre-seed funding to bridge the healthcare gap for African women, per Empower Africa coverage.
Ethiopia's digital health system credited with driving major gains in maternal and primary healthcare access.
TechCabal analysis frames Africa's femtech boom and its gaps, noting about 81% of funded femtech startups focus on pregnancy and fertility.
FemSTEM Pitch Competition 2026, run by the Africa Health Collaborative at Addis Ababa University with the Mastercard Foundation, offers up to USD 3,000 for women-led health startups.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: National strategy pairs reproductive health plans with an aggressive push to digitize community health, backed by a new startup law with explicit inclusion goals.

items.text: Reproductive Health Strategic Plan 2021-2025 sets priorities on maternal service utilization, family planning integration and adolescent SRH.
National Reproductive Health Commodity Security Strategy 2022-2026 targets reliable supply of family planning and RH commodities.
eCHIS, a Ministry of Health flagship, scales to nearly 8,000 health posts, digitizing RMNCH workflows for health extension workers.
Ethiopia enacts its landmark Startup Proclamation (No. 1396/2025), creating a Startup Innovation Fund and explicitly aiming to empower women-led startups and health tech.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Activity clusters around one flagship femtech platform, a resilient menstrual health manufacturing base, and accelerators beginning to court women-led health ventures.

items.text: YeneHealth expands its women-centered platform: period and pregnancy tracking, discreet e-pharmacy with delivery, telemedicine and culturally responsive SRH content, using AI and data analytics.
Mela for Her grows from startup to a 42-employee social enterprise (85%+ female), supplying reusable pads and menstrual underwear to 350,000+ women and girls via 179 female sales agents.
Mariam Seba Sanitary Products Factory, founded by Freweini Mebrahtu, produces about 750,000 pads a year, benefiting close to 800,000 girls and women.
Adey Pads, founded 2019 by Mikal Mamo, manufactures affordable 100% cotton reusable pads to fight period poverty in urban and rural Ethiopia.
Haftey, a Tigray-based social enterprise by and for women, combines menstrual health education, employment and reusable products.
FemSTEM Pitch Competition (Addis Ababa University Africa Health Collaborative + Mastercard Foundation) launches to fund women-led health startups.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: Deal flow is thin and early-stage, dominated by grants and pre-seed capital into YeneHealth plus development finance into menstrual health enterprises.
